Answer: B
Reason: Severe scoliosis (Cobb angle 50°) causes thoracic cage deformity that compresses the lung on the convex side of the curve (typically the right in common presentations), leading to atelectasis or shadowing and restrictive lung disease, which deteriorates respiratory function. Options suggesting improved function or equal expansion are physiologically incorrect for severe scoliosis with radiographic abnormalities.
